rules: not operationalisable: A combinatorial statement about losing-run length over 1,000 trades plus sizing and psychology advice. The run length is a function of the (unstated) win rate and of trade independence, not of anything in price; there is no concept-specific event whose edge vs a matched control could be measured, so none of trade/gate/rate test applies. The sizing rule (survive 5-10 full-risk losses) is pure arithmetic.

verdict_detail: A combinatorial statement about losing-run length over 1,000 trades plus sizing and psychology advice. The run length is a function of the (unstated) win rate and of trade independence, not of anything in price; there is no concept-specific event whose edge vs a matched control could be measured, so none of trade/gate/rate test applies. The sizing rule (survive 5-10 full-risk losses) is pure arithmetic.
notes: Arithmetic context (i.i.d. trades, N=1000, expected longest losing run): win 30%: ~16.0, win 40%: ~11.7, win 50%: ~9.0, win 60%: ~7.0, win 70%: ~5.4. So '5-10 in a row' holds for win rates of roughly 45-70%; at the typical 1R:2R book win rate (~33%) runs of 13+ are expected. Not a market claim.
